column1: Relationship between inflation  unemployment and labor force change rate in France: cointegration test

The thesis titled Relationship between inflation  unemployment and labor force change rate in France: Cointegration test by I.O. Kitov  O.I. Kitov  and S.A. Dolinskaya explores the intricate dynamics between inflation  unemployment  and labor force change rate in France. The authors propose a linear and lagged relationship model  expressed as π(t)=A0UE(t-t0)+A1dLF(t-t1)/LF(t-t1)+A2  where A0  A1  and A2 are empirical coefficients specific to the country. For France  these coefficients are determined as A0=-1  A1=4  A2=0.095  with time lags t0 and t1 both set at 4 years. This model  when applied to the GDP deflator  achieves a root mean square forecasting error (RMSFE) of 1.0% over a four-year horizon for the period from 1971 to 2004.

The study employs cointegration tests to validate the relationship  confirming that all three variables are integrated of order one. Two cointegration testing methods are utilized: the Engle-Granger approach  which involves a unit root test in the residuals of linear regression  and the Johansen cointegration rank test based on a VAR representation. Both methods affirm that the variables are cointegrated  supporting the long-run equilibrium relation previously identified.

The research further examines the relationships between inflation and labor force  and between unemployment and labor force  within specific time intervals unaffected by the Banque de France's monetary policy changes introduced in 1995. These individual relationships are also found to be cointegrated within their respective intervals.

The study also estimates VAR and vector error correction (VEC) models  which offer marginal improvements in RMSFE at the four-year horizon for both GDP deflator (down to 0.9%) and CPI (~1.1%) compared to the regression study results. The VECM approach allows for re-estimation of coefficients in both individual and generalized relationships between the variables for cointegration ranks 1 and 2.

A comparison between the standard cointegration approach and the integral approach for estimating coefficients in the relationships reveals the superiority of the latter. The integral approach  which uses cumulative inflation curves or indices  better predicts the evolution of price levels and is a powerful tool for identifying true relationships between non-stationary variables  potentially rejecting spurious regressions. Cumulative curves enhance the signal-to-noise ratio after differentiation and reduce dependence on the statistical properties of error terms.

The study concludes that the confirmed linear lagged relationship between inflation  unemployment  and labor force change indicates a misapplication of monetary policy by the Banque de France since 1995. The policy  which fixed monetary growth to a reference value of around 4.5%  resulted in unemployment rates twice as high as those dictated by the long-term equilibrium link to labor force change  compensating for the enforced price stability.

The thesis is organized into four sections  with the first section introducing the model and presenting results for France from previous studies. The second section focuses on estimating the order of integration in measured inflation  while subsequent sections delve into further analysis and implications of the findings.
